summary.text: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democrat, won the November 3, 2026 election for governor of Alaska, defeating Bernadette Wilson, Dave Bronson and Treg Taylor, according to unofficial results.
From Sitka, he served ten years in the Alaska House of Representatives and was a member of a bipartisan House coalition.
His campaign focused on school funding, fisheries and rebuilding the state ferry system, and he said he would fill his cabinet one-third each with Democrats, independents and Republicans.

paragraphs.text: Kreiss-Tomkins was born and raised in Sitka. He attended Yale University but dropped out to run for the Alaska House of Representatives.
He represented District 35 in Southeast Alaska from 2013 to 2023 and chaired the House State Affairs Committee in the 30th Legislature.

Late in his tenure he co-chaired a bipartisan working group on the state's fiscal crisis, whose recommendations were not implemented, and he was a member of the bipartisan fiscal working group that drafted a long-term fiscal plan in 2021.

He received 50.9% of first-choice votes to Wilson's 28.0%, Bronson's 13.6% and Taylor's 7.2%, according to unofficial results from the Alaska Division of Elections, and the Associated Press called the race for him.
